summary: Stop a step's execution clock while its seat waits for a build slot or the merge queue, within one 12-hour wait budget per attempt

replay.detail: Existing claims replay unchanged: none carries clock, wait_until_unix_ms or wait_ms. A member that runs older code rejects a work.progress claim with clock or wait_until_unix_ms at schema admission with unknown-claim-field, keeps the signed claim as a waiting unknown record, keeps syncing and projecting every claim it knows, and does not apply that wait or resume until it is upgraded; it never sees the wait, so it does not charge it to the execution clock either. The checkpoint planner replays the same timing fold; with no wait declared the fold equals the earlier one.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. A wait is a work.progress claim with the optional fields clock and wait_until_unix_ms; the step view gains optional execution fields that are omitted when empty.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention, authority or admission rule change and no rules-version change. The claim schema registry digest changes because work.* claims accept the two optional fields; the existing registry upgrade rules apply.

compatibility.detail: Adds the work actions wait and resume (st work wait --for DURATION --reason TEXT, st work resume), the optional work.progress claim fields clock and wait_until_unix_ms, and optional step view fields; the claim schema registry digest changes. Existing actions, claims and views are unchanged. A wait is accepted only from the holder of a live lease, needs a reason, and draws on 12 hours per step attempt; a request past the budget is refused with wait-budget-exhausted. An older daemon refuses a wait request as an unknown action. Nothing calls the new actions until a seat or the host build queue adopts them, and waits are safe to use only after every member that can fold step timing runs this build.

downtime.detail: No startup work or expected interruption; the change adds no store migration and no new background work beyond one reconciler wake at a wait's end.

manual.detail: No operator actions or configuration changes are required. Do not adopt the new actions, including the host cargo build-queue call to st work wait and st work resume, until every member that can fold step timing runs this build; that call is host configuration outside this repository.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or new swap-back restrictions. Upgrading an older member retries its held wait claims against the new registry and converges on the same graph (covered by a two-member mixed-build test). Rolling a member back leaves later wait claims as unknown records on it until it is upgraded again; waits recorded before the rollback stop being applied there, so a step on that member can time out sooner.
